title: A Orbit for the Gravity
premise: Hazel Joubert is a clone created to inherit the unfinished work of her original, murdered aboard the dying colony of Meridian's Reach — a case no court will reopen and no one left alive to solve. As she records the colony's slow, forgotten collapse, a distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct for two centuries, carrying proof that the war consuming the outer systems was started by the original Hazel's own discovery. Pursued by a military auditor who wants the signal buried and haunted by the original's memories bleeding into her own, Hazel must decode the message and broadcast it through the colony's last jump window. She succeeds at the cost of the colony's final transmitter — and of her own cover — ending the war but exposing every clone inheritance like hers, forcing her to claim a life she never asked for as her own.
about_author: Dominic Oyelaran is a former orbital-mechanics engineer who spent six years on decommissioning crews for failed lunar outposts before turning to fiction. His work explores inheritance, obsolescence, and the quiet dignity of places the galaxy has stopped watching.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dying Place
chapters.summary: Hazel Joubert opens her log on Meridian's Reach, cataloguing failing systems and the colony's dwindling population. Third-person limited, Hazel's POV. Establishes her clinical detachment and the emotional beat of loneliness disguised as duty.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Hazel reviews the legal documents of her creation: she inherits the original's property, debts, and her unsolved murder. Flashbacks to her decanting. POV Hazel. Beat: unease at being a legal fiction wearing a dead woman's name.

chapters.title: Case File 4471
chapters.summary: Hazel studies the original's murder investigation — three suspects, all dead or gone. POV Hazel. Beat: frustration at inheriting a puzzle designed to stay unsolved.

chapters.title: The Auditor Arrives
chapters.summary: A military transport makes an unscheduled landing; auditor Wren Okonkwo claims to be inspecting the colony's decommission status but watches Hazel too closely. POV Hazel. Beat: first intrusion of the outside war into her invisible life.

chapters.title: Salt and Static
chapters.summary: Colony elder Amara Diallo shows Hazel the greenhouse failing and admits the air scrubbers have months, not years. POV Amara. Beat: quiet grief of a community pretending to have a future.

chapters.title: Memories That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Hazel experiences her first memory bleed — the original's last evening, a corridor, a voice. POV Hazel. Beat: terror that her identity is a leaky vessel.

chapters.title: The Signal
chapters.summary: The colony's ancient receiver catches a repeating distress transmission — in Old Meridian, a language dead for two centuries. POV Hazel. Beat: electric wonder breaking through her numbness.

chapters.title: Decoding the Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Hazel uses the original's linguistic archives to begin translation; the message references coordinates and a phrase: 'the first shot was ours.' POV Hazel. Beat: dawning dread that the original found something worth killing for.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Wren interrogates Hazel about the original's research, revealing the military believes the original smuggled war-crimes evidence off-world. POV Wren. Beat: the auditor as believer, not villain — duty versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Colony Votes
chapters.summary: Amara convenes the remaining colonists; evacuation is offered and refused — they will die where they built. POV Amara. Beat: stubborn love for a place the galaxy abandoned.

chapters.title: Bleed-Through
chapters.summary: A second memory bleed: the original meeting a courier, hiding a data shard in the transmitter array. POV Hazel. Beat: the case and the signal begin to converge.

chapters.title: The Shard
chapters.summary: Hazel retrieves the data shard from the array housing and finds it encrypted with the original's biometric signature — hers. POV Hazel. Beat: the inheritance clause becomes literal; she is the key.

chapters.title: Two of One Name
chapters.summary: Hazel decrypts fragments: flight logs proving the war's opening strike was a false flag by the Core fleet. POV Hazel. Beat: vertigo of holding a truth that could end or ignite a war.

chapters.title: Wren's Report
chapters.summary: Wren drafts a recommendation to erase Meridian's Reach and its records; hesitates over Hazel's file, marked 'disposable asset.' POV Wren. Beat: conscience cracking against career.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Hazel calculates the last jump window in eleven days — the only time a broadcast from Meridian can reach the neutral relay at Ceres Deep. POV Hazel. Beat: a clock starts; invisibility has a deadline.

chapters.title: Amara's Confession
chapters.summary: Amara admits she knew the original was investigating the fleet and warned her to stop — guilt she has carried for years. POV Amara. Beat: the weight of surviving by staying silent.

chapters.title: The Third Suspect
chapters.summary: Hazel identifies the killer's likely identity: a fleet intelligence officer listed dead — whose shuttle transponder pinged the colony the night of the murder. POV Hazel. Beat: the murder case reopens itself.

chapters.title: Jamming
chapters.summary: The colony's uplink fails — sabotaged. Wren denies it; someone else is on-world. POV Hazel. Beat: paranoia; the hunter realizes she is hunted.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Hab Ring
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren, uneasy allies, track an intruder through the sealed sections of the colony. POV alternating. Beat: grudging respect between two women on opposite sides of duty.

chapters.title: Officer Vey
chapters.summary: They corner the intruder: Lieutenant Vey, the 'dead' officer, sent to destroy the shard and finish the original's murder. He wounds Wren and escapes with a decoy. POV Hazel. Beat: rage and grief; the case has a face.

chapters.title: Triage
chapters.summary: Hazel treats Wren's wound; Wren, feverish, confesses she was ordered to bury the evidence and chose instead to see it. POV Wren. Beat: love against duty — Wren chooses Hazel over the fleet.

chapters.title: What the Original Wanted
chapters.summary: A final memory bleed, the most complete: the original's plan to broadcast the truth herself, and her message to whoever she became. POV Hazel. Beat: the clone stops being an heir and becomes a continuation.

chapters.title: The Colony's Gift
chapters.summary: The colonists, learning everything, offer their last power reserves to charge the transmitter — shortening their own lives. POV Amara. Beat: the price of survival paid willingly.

chapters.title: Vey's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Vey broadcasts a demand: surrender the shard or the fleet will 'sanitize' the colony early. POV Hazel. Beat: the war arrives at her door with a countdown.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Vey's team destroys the backup reactor; two colonists die sealing the breach. POV Amara. Beat: grief hardening into resolve; the colony's death is no longer abstract.

chapters.title: The Decoy Transmission
chapters.summary: Hazel broadcasts a false signal to draw Vey's team to the far array. POV Hazel. Beat: the hunted becomes the strategist.

chapters.title: Corridor of the Original's Death
chapters.summary: Hazel lures Vey into the corridor from her memory bleeds and confronts him with the murder reconstructed. POV Hazel. Beat: the inherited case closed in the place it was opened.

chapters.title: Confession at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Vey admits the original died refusing to hand over the shard; Hazel records his confession before Wren, recovered, arrests him. POV Wren. Beat: justice, late but not absent.

chapters.title: Four Days to the Window
chapters.summary: Repairs race the clock; the transmitter needs a manual alignment no drone can survive. POV Hazel. Beat: the cost comes into focus — someone must stay.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren offers to take the alignment post; Hazel refuses — Wren is the witness the truth needs alive. POV Wren. Beat: love against duty, inverted — loving someone means sending them away.

chapters.title: Amara's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Amara teaches Hazel the colony's naming rite: the dead are not mourned, they are continued. POV Amara. Beat: Hazel accepts she is not a copy but a continuation.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Shadow
chapters.summary: A Core warship enters orbit, demanding surrender before the window. POV Hazel. Beat: the walls close in; the broadcast must happen under their guns.

chapters.title: Signal Jammed
chapters.summary: The warship jams all frequencies; the colony's only hope is the old deep-space array on the far side of the moon. POV Hazel. Beat: despair, then the memory of the original's contingency plan.

chapters.title: The Long Walk
chapters.summary: Hazel crosses the lunar surface to the array through a storm, guided by the original's memories of terrain she's never walked. POV Hazel. Beat: the two Hazels finally move as one.

chapters.title: Alignment
chapters.summary: Hazel manually aligns the array as the jump window opens; the warship's landing parties close in. POV Hazel. Beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Hazel transmits the full evidence — flight logs, Vey's confession, the original's message — in Old Meridian and Common, aimed at the neutral relay. POV Hazel. Beat: the climax; truth leaves her hands forever.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Orbit
chapters.summary: The warship withdraws under orders; the broadcast is propagating through the relay network. Wren testifies by open channel. POV Wren. Beat: relief shadowed by what it cost.

chapters.title: The Colony's Last Light
chapters.summary: The scrubbers fail; the colonists hold their naming rite as the station powers down. POV Amara. Beat: elegy — the price of survival, paid in full.

chapters.title: Hazel Joubert, Continued
chapters.summary: Hazel, evacuated with Wren, files the closed murder case and claims her name publicly as her own, not the original's. POV Hazel. Beat: inheritance accepted; identity chosen.

chapters.title: An Orbit for the Gravity
chapters.summary: Months later, the war ends in armistice; Hazel records a new log from a station above Meridian's Reach's silent hull, promising to remember. POV Hazel. Beat: resolution — gravity is what holds you to what you love, and she stays in orbit around it.
